hints: Sort applicants by desired size and apartments by actual size.
Compare the smallest unmatched applicant with the smallest apartment: if too small for the applicant, discard the apartment; if too large, discard the applicant.
If their sizes differ by at most k, match them and advance both.
analogy: Line up both sides by size and resolve the smallest waiting request with the smallest available apartment that could fit.
example: Desired sizes 45,60,80 and apartments 30,60,75 with k=5: only 60 matches 60, so the answer is 1.
algorithm: Sort both lists and use two pointers. Match when abs(a-b)<=k; otherwise advance the side whose current value is too small to match the other.
correctness: The smallest apartment can only match applicants whose acceptable interval includes it; when it is below the smallest applicant's interval, it cannot help anyone later, and the symmetric argument applies.
complexity: O(n log n + m log m) time and O(1) extra pointer space beyond sorting.
